After reacting with a Caravan Guard, you can use another one, even one you just drew, and also can use other Reactions, even ones you just drew; you keep going until you have no more Reactions you wish to respond to the Attack with.

If you call {card:Royal Carriage} on Caravan Guard after you play it as a Reaction during another player's turn, it will stay in play until your next turn and give you an extra {coin:+1} at that time, as you would expect. However, if you call {card:Coin of the Realm}, it will be discarded during the Clean-up phase of the Attacking player's turn, and the +2 Actions it will give you don't do anything for you, as +Action doesn't mean anything when it's not your turn.
If you react with this against a {card:Relic}, you draw a card, and then you put your -1 Card token on your deck.

If you react with a {card:Training|Trained} Caravan Guard against a {card:Bridge Troll}, and you don't have your -1 Coin token, you will get {coin:+1} before you take your -1 Coin token, so you won't be able to remove it. But if you get affected by a different attack afterwards, reacting with a Trained Caravan Guard will remove your -1 Coin token.
This gives each other player their -1 coin token, which will cause those players to get {cost:1} less the next time they get {cost:}; see the Tokens section.
It also gives you +1 Buy both on the turn you play it and on your next turn, and lowers costs of cards by {cost:1} on both of those turns (but not less than {cost:0}).
The cost lowering applies to all cards everywhere, including cards in the Supply, in hand, and in decks.
It's cumulative; for example if you play two Bridge Trolls, and on your next turn play another Bridge Troll, then {card:Duchy} would cost {cost:2}.
If you play this twice with {card:Throne Room}, cards cost {cost:2} less both this turn and next turn.
This gives each other player their -1 coin token, which will cause those players to get {cost:1} less the next time they get {cost:}; see the Tokens section.
It also gives you +1 Buy both on the turn you play it and on your next turn.
While Bridge Troll is in play, on your turns only, cards cost {cost:1} less, but not less than {cost:0}.
This applies to all cards everywhere, including cards in the Supply, cards in hand, and cards in Decks.

children.text: For example if you have Bridge Troll in play and play {card:Raze}, trashing {card:Estate}, Estate will only cost {cost:1}, so you will only look at one card rather than two.

items.text: This is cumulative; if you have two Bridge Trolls in play from last turn and play another Bridge Troll this turn, all cards will cost {cost:3} less this turn (to a minimum of {cost:0}).
Bridge Troll's cost reduction, unlike some other cost reducers, is contingent on the Bridge Troll being in the play area. This has several consequences:

children.text: If you play the same Bridge Troll multiple times on the same turn (e.g., with Throne Room), you don't get costs reduced twice, since only one Bridge Troll is actually in play.
If a Bridge Troll is removed from the play area prematurely (e.g., with {card:Bonfire}), its cost reduction ends.

If you play Bridge Troll under the influence of {card:Enchantress} or a Way, you still get the cost reduction in addition to the effects of Enchantress or the Way. However, since the Bridge Troll's next-turn ability is overruled in these cases, it will be discarded from play at the end of the current turn, and so its cost reduction ends then.

items.text: When you discard this from play (normally, in the Clean-up phase of the turn you played it), you get {debt:6}, and then get an extra opportunity to pay off {debt:} with {cost:}, right then.
You do not get the {debt:6} if you did not discard it from play - for example, if you trash it due to {card:Counterfeit} (from Dominion: Dark Ages).
You only get {debt:6} per copy of Capital discarded; for example if you use {card:Crown} to play Capital twice, you still only get {debt:6} when you discard it from play.

Even if Capital is subject to the {card:Highwayman} Attack, or the effect of {card:Enlightenment}, making it give no {cost:} when you play it, you still take the {debt:6} when you discard it from play.
Rising Sun updated the rules for Debt, allowing you to pay off debt at any time during your turn, making the text about paying off debt during Clean-up redundant.
You can look through your discard pile even if you know there are no {card:Settlers} in it.
The card you set aside doesn't have to be the next card you gain; you could gain multiple cards and then gain one where you decided to set it aside.
If you don't set a card aside at all, Cargo Ship is discarded that turn.

If you haven't set aside a card by Cargo Ship's ability, Cargo Ship is set to be discarded this turn, which means you may use {card:Improve} to trash it during Clean-up and gain a different card. If you do, you may then still use Cargo Ship's ability and set aside the newly gained card for next turn, however since Cargo Ship is no longer [[in play], it will not move the set-aside card to your hand at the start of your next turn. Instead, the card stays set-aside for the rest of the game, but still counts for things like {card:Gardens} during scoring.
To be affected, a card must have a {coin:+} amount in its text, not just a {cost:} amount - for example, Capitalism turns {card:Improve} into a Treasure, but does not affect {card:Inventor}.
Having Capitalism means you can play any number of Action cards with {coin:+} amounts in your Buy phase (without using up Action plays).

It also means that things that interact with Treasure cards also interact with those cards; for example, if you have Capitalism, you can use {card:Treasurer} to gain an Improve from the trash, since Improve is a Treasure on your turns.
Any time you play an Action - Treasure card, it is both an Action and a Treasure, regardless of which phase it is.
Getting +1 Action in your Buy phase does not let you play other Action cards then.

Capitalism works on your turn, but affects cards everywhere; for example if you have Capitalism and play {card:Bandit}, you could trash another player's Improve, and it is not relevant if that player has Capitalism or not.
A card with {coin:+} in its text becomes a Treasure even if it does not give you {coin:+} when you play it. For instance:

children.text: {card:Aristocrat} only gives you {coin:+3} under relatively restricted circumstances depending on how many other Aristocrats are in play, but if you have Capitalism, Aristocrat is a Treasure at all times during your turn, regardless of how many Aristocrats are in play.
With Capitalism you could play a {card:Steward} during your Buy phase and use it to trash two cards, receiving no {coin:+}.
{card:Caravan Guard} becomes a Treasure even though it only gives {coin:+} on a future turn.

items.text: Things that are not Action cards do not become Treasures even if they have {coin:+} in their text, such as {card:Raider}.

{card:Druid} does not become a Treasure even if one of the Boons it controls gives {coin:+}; what matters is the text of the Druid card itself. Similarly, a Way that gives {coin:+} such as {card:Way of the Seal} has no effect on which cards are subject to Capitalism.
Since Capitalism changes the number of types a card has, that will affect how it interacts with cards such as {card:Courtier} and {card:Falconer}.
During your turns, all cards, including cards in the Supply, in hands, and in Decks, cost {cost:1} less, but not less than {cost:0}.
For example if you have Canal and play {card:Villain}, other players discard a card costing at least {cost:2}, which could not be {card:Estate}, as Estate only costs {cost:1} on your turns.
At the end of the game, it is no longer your turn, so Canal does not affect scoring for {card:Plateau Shepherds}.
There is no official FAQ for Captain.
You choose a non-Duration, non-Command Action card from the Supply that costs up to {cost:4} and play it, leaving it there, then choose again at the start of your next turn.
On the second turn, you can choose to play a different card, or the same card if there is still a copy of it in the Supply.

Captain can only play a visible card in the Supply, and the top card of a pile; it cannot play a card from an empty pile, or a card that has not been uncovered from a split pile, or a card from a split pile that has been bought out, or a non-Supply card (such as {card:Mercenary}).
The Action card stays in the Supply; if an effect tries to move it (such as {card:Island} putting itself on your Island Mat) it will fail to move it.

Captain can play a card that trashes itself when played; if the card checks to see if it was trashed (such as {card:Mining Village}), it was not, but if the card does not check (such as {card:Acting Troupe}), it will function normally.
Cards that normally move other cards from the Supply can move themselves when played via Captain; for example playing {card:Workshop} can gain itself, and playing {card:Lurker} can trash itself.

If there are no non-Duration, non-Command Action cards in the Supply that cost up to {cost:4} the turn you play Captain, Captain still stays in play and tries to play a card at the start of your next turn.
While Captain can't directly play Duration cards, it can still stay in play for longer than usual if, on the second turn, it plays a {card:Throne Room} that then plays a {card:Caravan}.
First you get +1 Action and Exile a card from your hand; this is not optional.
Then if that is the only copy of that card that you have in Exile, you get {coin:+3}.
If you can't Exile a card, you don't get {coin:+3}.
When you play this, you Exile a non-Victory card from the Supply; when you gain this, you Exile a {card:Gold} from the Supply.
If an attacked player reveals two cards each costing from {cost:3} to {cost:6}, that player chooses which card they Exile.
For example, if you trash an {card:Estate}, which costs {cost:2}, you could choose to get +2 Cards, or +2 Actions, or {coin:+2}, or +2 Favors.
If you trash a card with {debt:} or {potion} in the cost (from other expansions), you get nothing for those symbols.
First draw a card and get +2 Actions.

Then decide if you want to discard 2 cards for {coin:+2}. You may choose to do this even with fewer than 2 cards in hand, and will discard what you can, but you only get {coin:+2} if you actually discarded 2 cards.

Then decide if you want to spend {cost:2} for +2 Cards. The {cost:2} can come from discarding to Capital City, or some other source, e.g. a {card:Barbarian} you played earlier in the turn. You don't get to play Treasures here to make the {cost:2} though.
If you play this with {card:Way of the Chameleon}, you may discard 2 cards for +2 Cards. You can also pay {cost:2} for {coin:+2}, although this isn't useful.
Once you buy this, the ability is mandatory.
You cannot search through your discard pile prior to buying this Event to check if you want to buy it.
When you gain this, you have to play it; it's not optional.
The cards go to your hand after drawing your regular hand of 5 cards for next turn.

children.text: For example you might set aside two {card:Estate|Estates} and two {card:Copper|Coppers} on a Cage on an early turn; then on a late turn, buy a {card:Province}, trash the Cage, and add the two Estates and two Coppers to your hand at end of turn.

items.text: See the Additional rules section for Duration cards in Dominion: Plunder regarding things happening "the next time".
If you set aside nothing with this, it will still stay in play until you gain a Victory card.

If gaining a Victory card causes you to play this (e.g. you gain a Province, then gain a Cage with {card:Haggler}, and play it with {card:Mining Road}), that won't trigger the Cage (it triggers off the next Victory card you gain).
You can trash a Cabin Boy to gain another Cabin Boy.
For example if you revealed 3 {card:Copper|Coppers} and a {card:Farmhands}, you'd put one Copper and the Farmhands into your hand, and discard the other two Coppers.
Shuffle if necessary to get 4 cards to reveal; if there still aren't 4 cards, reveal what you can.
This includes cards gained from outside the Supply (such as Loot, from Plunder).
Cards with {debt:} costs don't cost exactly {cost:0}, and so come with a {card:Copper}.
Choose any number of cards from your hand; discard them all at once; then draw as many cards as you actually discarded.
If this causes you to shuffle, you will shuffle in the cards you discarded.
You do not have to let players see any but the top card discarded; however the number of cards you discard is public.
You cannot discard the Cellar itself, since it is not in your hand after you play it.
You can't discard Cellar to itself, since it isn't in your hand any longer when you resolve it.
You choose what cards to discard and discard them all at once. You only draw cards after you have discarded.
If you have to shuffle to do the drawing, the discarded cards will end up shuffled into your new Deck.
You cannot trash the Chapel itself, since it is not in your hand after you play it.

You don't have to trash any cards; zero is included in "up to four". This may be relevant if you are forced to play Chapel (for example, as a result of playing {card:Herald}) and don't have anything you want to trash.
When you trash any cards with "when you trash this" abilities, you trash all the cards first, then pick an order to resolve things that happen due to trashing them.
You can't trash the Chapel itself since it isn't in your hand when you resolve it.
You could trash a different Chapel card if that card were in your hand.

You must resolve the Chancellor (decide whether or not to discard your Deck by flipping it into your Discard pile) before doing other things on your turn, like deciding what to buy or playing another Action card.
You may not look through your Deck as you discard it.

Putting your deck in your discard pile in this manner does not count as individually discarding each card in your deck, and you may not use Reactions that require discarding a card (such as that of {card:Tunnel|Tunnels}) as you put those cards in your discard pile with Chancellor.
You draw a card and get +2 Actions no matter what.
If there is just one empty pile in the Supply, you also draw another card.
If there are two or more empty piles, you both draw another card, and get {coin:+1} and +1 Buy.
There are no further bonuses if three or more piles are empty.
This only checks how many piles are empty when you play it; what you got does not change if a pile becomes empty (or non-empty, such as due to {card:Encampment} from Empires).
This only counts Supply piles, not non-Supply piles like {card:Spoils} from Dark Ages.

Unlike {card:Laboratory}, if you play this when a pile is empty, you draw a card, then draw a second card separately. So if you only have 1 card in your deck, you can see that card before shuffling and topdecking a card with {card:Star Chart}.
You draw a card and get +2 Actions no matter what.
If there is just one empty pile in the Supply, you also draw another card.
If there are two or more empty piles, you both draw another card, and get {coin:+1} and +1 Buy.
There are no further bonuses if three or more piles are empty.
This only checks how many piles are empty when you play it; what you got does not change if a pile becomes empty (or non-empty, such as due to {card:Ambassador} from Dominion: Seaside).
This only counts Supply piles, not non-Supply piles like Spoils from Dark Ages.
You draw a card and can play two more Actions no matter what.
If there is just one empty pile in the Supply, you also draw another card.
If there are two or more empty piles, you both draw another card, and get {cost:1} to spend and an extra Buy to use in the Buy phase.
There are no further bonuses if three or more piles are empty.
This only checks how many piles are empty when you play it; if piles become empty later in the turn, you do not go back and get the bonuses.
If a pile stops being empty due to cards being returned to it, such as with the Dominion: Seaside card Ambassador, Cities played after that will not count that pile as empty.
An empty trash pile does not count for this.
When you play this, you look at the top three cards of your deck, and either put all three into your hand, or discard all three and draw the next three cards.
If you discard them and have to shuffle to draw three cards, you will shuffle in the cards you discarded and may end up drawing some of them.
When you trash Catacombs, you gain a card costing less than it.
This happens whether Catacombs is trashed on your turn or someone else's, and no matter who has the card that trashed it.

Putting the 3 cards you're looking at into your hand will have no interaction with your -1 Card token and/or {card:Way of the Chameleon}. But if you discard those 3 cards, then the +3 Cards will be affected by your -1 Card token and/or Way of the Chameleon.

If you play this with {card:Elder} and choose both its options, you won't get anything useful. You'll put the 3 cards you're looking at into your hand, but then you'll still discard them and draw 3 different cards.
When you trash this with e.g. {card:Remodel}, you gain a card from Catacombs before you gain a card with Remodel.
When you play this, you look at the top 3 cards of your deck, and either put all 3 into your hand, or discard all 3 and draw the next 3 cards.
If you discard them and have to shuffle to draw 3 cards, you will shuffle in the cards you discarded and may end up drawing some of them.
When you trash Catacombs, you gain a card costing less than it.
This happens whether Catacombs is trashed on your turn or someone else's, and no matter who has the card that trashed it.
The gained card comes from the Supply and is put into your discard pile.
You draw a card first, then look at the top 4 cards of your deck.
If there are fewer than 4 cards left (even after shuffling), just look at as many as you can.
Discard any number of the cards you looked at - none, all four, or something in-between - and put the rest back on top of your deck in any order.
You do not reveal any of the cards, except whatever ends up on top of your discard pile.
Even though the official FAQ uses the word "reveal", the discarded cards aren't revealed, meaning that Reactions like {card:Patron} are not activated.

If you happen to put a card on top of your deck in the middle of resolving Cartographer—for instance, by discarding a {card:Tunnel}, gaining a {card:Gold}, and top-decking it due to {card:Progress}—then when you return the looked-at cards to your deck they will go on top of the card you just put there.
You draw a card first, then look at the top 4 cards of your deck.
If there are fewer than 4 cards left in your deck, look at the remaining cards, and shuffle your discard pile (which does not include those cards) to get the remainder needed to look at.
If there are still not enough cards, just look at as many as you can.
Discard any number of the cards you looked at - none, all four, or something in-between - and put the rest back on top of your deck in any order.
If there were no cards left in your deck, these become the only cards in your deck.
You do not reveal the cards you put back.
Champion stays in play for the rest of the game once played.

For the rest of the game, it provides you with an additional +1 Action each time you play an Action, which means you will always be able to play all of your Actions; and it protects you from all further Attacks played (whether you want the protection or not).
Champion only protects you from Attacks played after it; for example it does not stop a previously played {card:Swamp Hag} from giving you {card:Curse|Curses} that turn.

Champion does not protect you from the effects of cards that are not of the Attack type, such as {card:Possession} and {card:Masquerade}; the effects of cards that are not the result of them being played, such as the effect of buying {card:Noble Brigand}; or the effects of landscapes that have attack-like abilities, such as {card:Circle of Witches}.
If you remove Champion from play (such as by playing it with {card:Throne Room} and using {card:Way of the Horse} for one of these plays), it will have no effect after the end of the current turn.

Although ordinarily Champion makes it impossible to run out of Actions, {card:Snowy Village} can overrule that. If you play Snowy Village, then for the rest of the turn, Champion will not give you the expected extra Action for each Action card you play, and so you can run out.
Cards with multiple types that include Action, such as {card:Crown}, are Actions.

If the card you trash is a Treasure, each other player discards down to 3 cards in hand; if the card you trash costs {cost:3} or more, each other player gains a {card:Curse}; if it is both (e.g. {card:Silver}), both things happen; if it is neither, neither thing happens.
If you have no cards in hand left to trash, neither thing happens.

Unlike {card:Followers} (where one player gains the {card:Curse} and discards before the next player does so), the other players first gain the Curse in turn order, and then the other players discard cards in turn order.
You and the player to your left reveal your top cards; yours goes into your hand, theirs goes back on their deck.
If your card cost more you get {coin:+1} and {vp:+1}; you can put the {vp:} token on the Chariot Race to remind you that it made {coin:+1} this turn.
If it is a tie, your card did not cost more.
With {debt:}, your card costs more only if both {cost:} and {debt:} amounts are larger, or one is larger and the other the same.

children.text: For example {card:Fortune} ({cost:8}{debt:8}) costs more than {card:Overlord} ({debt:8}), but Overlord does not cost more than {card:Silver}, and Silver does not cost more than Overlord.

items.text: If either player has no card to reveal, your card does not cost more.
{potion} cards never cost more or less than cards costing {debt:}.

Just like {debt:}-costs, {potion} cards only cost more than another card if both the {cost:} and {potion} amounts are larger, or one is larger and one the same. This means that {card:Familiar} costs more than {card:Farmers' Market} and {card:Apothecary}, but it does not cost more than {card:Forum}.
If you have you -1 card token or if you choose to play Chariot Race as {card:Way of the Chameleon}, you will not draw or reveal any card, and thus cannot have the higher cost.
These are cumulative, and each Charm does not have to gain a different card, just a different card from the one whose gain triggered the Charms' effect.

children.text: For example if you play two Charms and then gain a {card:Forum}, the Charms could gain you two {card:Duchy|Duchies}.

items.text: If the next card you gain triggers other on-gain effects, you can choose the order of those effects and the additional card you gain from Charm.

children.text: For example if you play Charm, choosing to gain an extra card, and then gain {card:Villa}, you may put the Villa in your hand, get +1 Action, and return to your Action phase either before or after gaining an additional card costing {cost:4}.

items.text: The costs have to be identical; for example if you play Charm and buy {card:Overlord}, you can gain {card:City Quarter}, which also costs {debt:8}, but not {card:Fortune}, which costs {cost:8}{debt:8}.

If the next card you gain changes its own cost, that can affect what Charm can gain. For example, if you play 2 Charms (both choosing the 2nd option) and then gain a {cost:6}-cost {card:Destrier}, the first Charm gains a {cost:5}-cost card, and the second Charm gains a {cost:4}-cost card.
If you gain a {card:Knights|Knight}, Charm can gain the next Knight from the pile (unless either of them are {card:Sir Martin}).
If you gain a Charm, play it with {card:Mining Road}, and choose the 2nd option, Charm won't trigger off of its own gain (it will trigger off your *next* gain).
These are cumulative, and each Charm does not have to gain a different card, just a different card from the one bought.

children.text: For example if you play two Charms and buy a Forum, you could gain two Duchies.

items.text: The card gained from Charm is gained before gaining the card you bought, which may matter when cards do things when gained.

children.text: For example if you buy Villa and gain {card:Rocks} via Charm, you will first gain a {card:Silver} to your deck due to Rocks, then get +1 Action and return to your Action phase due to Villa.

items.text: The costs have to be identical; for example if you play Charm and buy Overlord, you can gain City Quarter, which also costs {debt:8}, but not Fortune, which costs {cost:8}{debt:8}.

If the card you buy changes its own cost, that can affect which card Charm can gain. So if you play 2 Charms and then buy a {card:Destrier} for {cost:6}, then the first Charm gains a card costing {cost:6}, and the second charm gains a card costing {cost:5}.

Charm gains you a card *before* you gain the card you actually bought. This means that if you buy a {card:Knights|Knight}, you can't use Charm to gain the next Knight, because it hasn't been revealed yet at that point.
In games using this, replace one of your starting {card:Copper|Coppers} with a {card:Haunted Mirror}.
When you gain a Cemetery, trash from zero to four cards from your hand.
When Changeling is in the Supply, any time you gain a card costing at least {cost:3}, you may exchange it for a Changeling from the Supply.
You can only do this if you can actually return the card you gained, and there is at least one Changeling in the Supply.
The Changeling goes to your discard pile, no matter where the gained card went.
Things that happen due to gaining the gained card still happen.

children.text: So for example you could gain {card:Skulk}, exchange it for a Changeling (returning Skulk to the Supply and putting Changeling into your discard pile), and still gain a {card:Gold} from Skulk's ability.

items.text: Exchanging for a Changeling is optional.

You cannot do it if the gained card costs less than {cost:3}, even if it normally costs {cost:3} or more, and you cannot do it if the cost is neither more or less than {cost:3} (such as {card:Transmute} from Alchemy).

When you play Changeling, you trash it and gain a copy of a card you have in play; that can be any card you have in play, including Actions, Treasures, and Night cards, and including Duration cards you played on a previous turn that are still in play.

Changeling cannot gain a copy of Changeling, since it is not in play when the effect happens - it's either in the trash (in a normal turn) or set aside (when played in a {card:Possession|Possessed} turn).

You can choose any card you have in play, but if that card's pile is empty, or its name does not match the name of the top card on that pile (e.g. it's a split pile), or that card's pile is not in the Supply (e.g. {card:Imp}), or that card has no pile (e.g. an Heirloom, you gain nothing.

You can exchange for Changeling when gaining non-Supply cards, as long as they come from a pile, such as {card:Ghost}. You cannot exchange for non-Supply cards that do not have an associated pile, such as the Zombies.

You can still exchange for Changeling even if the Changeling pile is not in the Supply, for example if it is the pile chosen for {card:Ferryman}. However you cannot exchange for Changeling if it has no pile, e.g. when Changeling is in the {card:Black Market} deck.

Remember that you can choose the order in which simultaneous effects happen. When you gain a card that either gains other cards (like Skulk above) or moves itself (like {card:Villa}), and you allow that gaining or moving effect to happen first, Changeling will lose track of the card and not be able to exchange with it. If you want to exchange, make sure you do that first.

This checks the cost of the card as you're gaining it, not after. So if you gain a {card:Fisherman} with an empty discard pile, you cannot exchange it for a Changeling, because Fisherman cost {cost:2} when you gained it.
If you gain a Loot and exchange it for a Changeling, the Loot goes back on top of the pile, face down.
Exchanging is not gaining, so exchanging a card for a Changeling will not allow you to take Changelings out of exile.
Once you've claimed this ability, it is not optional.

This can affect an Action card played outside of the Action phase, if it is your first Action card played that turn; for example if you also had {card:Capitalism}, you could opt to play a {card:Flag Bearer} in your Buy phase as your first play of the turn, and it would still be played twice.
Citadel can cause a Duration card to be played twice; you will have to remember that on your next turn.

Like most other Throne Room variants, Citadel will still replay the Action card even if it is no longer in the play area after the first time it gets played (e.g., if it is a one-shot such as {card:Acting Troupe}. If this happens, the Action card is not moved back to the play area but its instructions are followed a second time.
If the first Action card you play is affected by {card:Enchantress}, you get +1 Card and +1 Action, then Citadel replays the card for its normal ability.

You can use Citadel's ability on the turn you buy it if you play your first Action card after buying Citadel. (This can happen, for instance, if you return to your Action phase by buying something like {card:Villa} after buying Citadel, or if you play a {card:Werewolf} during your Night phase.)
If you play a card, but then play a second card before you follow the first card's instructions, Citadel still replays the first card.
Once you have claimed this ability, it is not optional.
There is no way to remove your cube.
First you draw a card; then you put any card from your hand onto your deck.
There is no official FAQ for Church.
You may set aside zero, one, two, or three cards from your hand. Put them face down; you may look at them.
No matter how many cards you set aside, you may trash a card at the start of your next turn and Church is discarded at the end of that turn.
The card you trash can be a card you had set aside, or a card that was already in your hand.

If you play multiple Churches (or one Church multiple times such as via {card:Throne Room}), you may set aside multiple batches of up to three cards. What happens on your next turn is this: you put one batch of set-aside cards in hand, then trash, then put the next batch of set-aside cards in hand, then trash. You can choose which batch of set-aside cards you put in hand first.
When you gain Cavalry in your Buy phase, you get +2 Cards, +1 Buy, and return to your Action phase.
When you gain Cavalry in a different phase or during another player's turn, you get +2 Cards and +1 Buy.

items.text: When you play this, you put it on your Tavern mat.
It stays on your mat until you call it.
You can call it when gaining a card costing up to {cost:6}, and gain another copy of that card.
The gained card comes from the Supply and is put into your discard pile; Duplicate cannot gain non-supply cards such as {card:Teacher}.

Duplicate can be called during other players' turns when you gain cards; for example, another player might buy {card:Messenger} and choose to have each player gain an {card:Estate}, and you could Duplicate that Estate.
You can call multiple Duplicates to gain multiple copies of the same card.
Duplicate is discarded during the Clean-up of the turn you call it, whether or not it is your turn.
Cards with {potion} or {debt:} in their cost cannot be Duplicated.

If you have {card:Innovation}, which allows you to play a card immediately on gaining it, you could gain a Duplicate, play it immediately and put it on the Tavern mat, and then call it immediately to gain another Duplicate. This is because when the Duplicate reaches the Tavern mat, you're still within the time window of carrying out effects triggered by gaining the Duplicate.
When you play this, you get +1 Action, draw 2 cards, and discard 2 cards; then at the start of your next turn, you draw 2 cards and discard 2 cards.
Players revealing a card like {card:Moat} when this is played have to do it right then, not later, even though the attack will not hurt them until their turn.
While this is in play, the first Action each other player plays on each of their turns* will give them +1 Card +1 Action instead of what it would have normally done.
This does not affect abilities below a dividing line; they still function.

items.text: It can be helpful to turn the affected card sideways, to remember that it did not do what it normally did.

Enchantress does not affect card abilities from cards played on previous turns; for example if an opponent plays Enchantress and you have an {card:Archive} out from a previous turn, on your turn you will first get a card from your Archive as normal, and then the first Action card actually played on that turn will be affected by Enchantress.

If Enchantress affects a {card:Crown} played in a Buy phase, its player gets +1 Card +1 Action, but has no way to use the +1 Action, since it is their Buy phase (but it might matter e.g. if the player buys {card:Villa}).
If your opponents play multiple Enchantresses in a round, they still only affect the first card you play on each turn, and not any further cards.
* The rulebook now clarifies that opponents' extra turns will also be Enchanted.

† Many cards, including {card:Groundskeeper}, got {card:Groundskeeper|reworded} in 2022 and no longer have dividing lines. However, other cards still have dividing line effects (e.g. {card:Page} and {card:Urchin}), and those effects will still work, even if Enchanted.

Just like a {card:Crown} played during your Buy phase, if the first Action you play during a turn is a {card:Werewolf} at Night, you'll still get +1 Card and +1 Action (and have no way to use the +1 Action).
If a player under the effect of an Enchantress takes one or more extra turns, the first Action played on each of those turns is also turned into a cantrip.
If a Duration card gets affected by Enchantress, it will get discarded from play this turn. This doesn't stop any below-the-line effects.

Enchantress does not change anything about the card, it just prevents on-play instructions on the card from being carried out properly. So cards that are Enchanted can still activate Reactions (such as another player's {card:Diplomat}), still carry out all Adventures tokens effects (such as the +1 coin token from {card:Training}), and can still be replayed (e.g. by {card:Royal Carriage}) to perform their normal effects.
Enchantress, {card:Highwayman}, and Ways make you ignore an Action's instructions. Because they have the same timing, you can choose which of those effects will win.

children.text: However, Way of the Chameleon still makes you follow the Action's instructions, which means Enchantress will stop it (and you'll get +1 Card and +1 Action).

If you exchange the {card:Province} via {card:Trader} or {card:Changeling}, you still get {vp:+9}. But if you {card:Possession|Possess} a player and make them buy Dominate, no one gets {vp:+9}.
This counts Action cards in play, including Action cards played this turn, Duration cards in play from previous turns, and Reserve cards (from Dominion: Adventures) called into play this turn.

Since the attempt to gain {vp:2} (and thus, the check to see how many Actions are in play) has "when-gain" timing, if another effect with "when-gain" timing brings more Actions into play (such as {card:Duplicate} being called), the player can choose to resolve the effect bringing the Actions into play *first*, delaying the attempted {vp:} gain until after those effects are resolved. This can lead to instances where when an Emporium is first gained, fewer than 5 Actions are in play, but the player still gets {vp:2}, since they have chosen to do so after bringing a sufficient amount of Actions into play. For example, with only four Actions in play, a player could buy an Emporium, choose to call Duplicate first, then gain {vp:2} (since they now have 5 Actions in play), then another {vp:2} from the Duplicated Emporium.
Revealing a {card:Plunder} or {card:Gold} is optional.
When you return Encampment to the Supply, it goes on top of its pile, potentially covering up a Plunder.

If you cannot return Encampment to the Supply (e.g. you bought it from the {card:Black Market}), then if it is set aside it will stay there but will still count as one of your cards at the end of the game.
If you somehow play this at the start of Clean-up, and it sets itself aside, it will immediately return to the Supply.
Engineer cannot gain copies of itself, or any other card with {debt:} in the cost.
When you play it, you gain a card, then may trash Engineer to gain a second card (which can be the same as the first or different).
Donate happens before anything else that happens at the start of your turn, such as taking a card from {card:Archive}.
Effects that happen due to trashing cards (such as {card:Rocks|Rocks'}) will happen before you shuffle.
The start of your turn is during your Action phase.
If trashing cards draws you cards that were somehow not already in your hand, it is too late to trash those, and you will shuffle them into your deck.
Anything that cares about shuffling (such as {card:Star Chart}) happens when you shuffle your hand into your deck.
You only shuffle your hand into your deck; any cards that get into your discard pile (such as with {card:Order of Masons} or when reacting with {card:Market Square}) stay there.
You draw 5 cards no matter how many you had in hand before Donate.
Donate doesn't happen if the game ends first.
If you use {card:Possession} to control a turn where Donate happens, you choose what they trash, and those cards are set aside until after they draw their next hand.
Effects that happen due to trashing cards (such as Rocks') will happen before you shuffle.

This happens between turns, and so Possession (from Dominion: Alchemy) will no longer be doing anything.
The game ends at the end of a turn; it cannot end between turns.

children.text: If the game ends the same turn you buy Donate, then the game is over and Donate's effect will not happen after that turn. The exception is if any player has bought {card:Fleet}, which will keep the game going.

If sufficient piles to end the game are emptied during Donate's effect (such as by trashing {card:Hunting Grounds} or {card:Catacombs}), the next player takes their turn and then you check if the game still ends.

items.text: Cards played between turns (for example by trashing a Hunting Grounds to gain a {card:Duchy} and play {card:Sheepdog}) are discarded during the next Clean-up that happens (whether or not it's your turn or not).
If you activate an ability that grants you an extra turn, such as playing {card:Outpost}, on the same turn you buy Donate, the Donate effect happens before the extra turn.
If you gain the first {card:Province} on the same turn you buy Donate, you can choose the order of the effects of Donate and {card:Mountain Pass}.

Remember that you draw your normal hand during Clean-up before this. This means that if you drew fewer cards than normal during Clean-up (due to Outpost or your -1 Card token), or drew more cards than normal (due to {card:Flag} or {card:Expedition}), Donate will reset it to 5 cards afterwards.

If cards end up in your discard pile while Donating (e.g. you discard a {card:Market Square} and gain a {card:Gold}), Donate doesn't shuffle them into your deck (although they may get reshuffled when you draw +5 Cards at the end of resolving Donate).
If you trash a {card:Fortress} with Donate, it goes into the trash, then goes back to your hand, and then you shuffle your hand into your deck.
Cards you gain or trash during Donate are not counted as cards gained or trashed "on your turn", which matters for cards like {card:Smugglers}, {card:Treasure Hunter}, or {card:Goatherd}.
Since it's no longer your turn when Donating, cost reduction (like {card:Bridge}) stops having any effect when Donating. This may matter if you want to trash a {card:Catacombs}.

{card:Travelling Fair} can be used to get an early Druid on a 4 coin start, useful for boons such as {card:The Sky's Gift}.

You can play an Action card with no "choose" ability; it will simply do what it normally does.

If you play one with a "choose" ability, you may take an extra choice, but don't have to; for example, when playing {card:Count} (from Dark Ages), you could choose to only get one thing from the first "choose" ability, but two from the second.

If you choose multiple things, you do those things in the order listed on the card; for example, if you use Elder on {card:Blacksmith} and choose "draw until you have 6 cards in hand" and "+1 Card and +1 Action," you first draw up to 6, then get +1 Card and +1 Action.
If you use Elder on {card:Courtier} (from Intrigue), you get one extra choice, not one extra choice per type.

Elder doesn't affect all choices, just ones that say "choose" and have a list of options; for example {card:Workshop} gives you a choice of what card to gain, but Elder playing Workshop doesn't do anything extra.
Some cards may appear like they're giving you a choice (e.g. {card:Weaver}, {card:Barge}, and {card:Jester}), but because they don't say "choose", they aren't affected by Elder.
If you use Elder on {card:Scrap} and trash a card costing {cost:0}, you get one choice. But if you use Elder on Scrap and trash nothing (because you have no cards in hand), you get no choices.
Elder does not make {card:Catacombs} more useful: If you choose both options, you put the 3 cards into your hand, discard them (from your hand), and draw 3 different cards.

Normally, Elder will have no effect on Duration cards that give you a choice next turn. For example, if you use Elder on {card:Amulet}, you get an additional choice this turn, but you won't get an additional choice on the following turn. And if you use Elder on {card:Cabin Boy}, nothing special happens. Elder won't stay in play with the Duration.

children.text: However, if you play an Elder at the start of your turn (e.g. with {card:Contract}) and have it play a {card:Quartermaster}), you can choose both its options this turn (but not on future turns).

items.text: If you use Elder on {card:Stronghold}, you can get both {coin:+3} now and +3 Cards next turn. Elder won't stay in play with the Stronghold.
If you use Elder on an Action that gives choices, and then you replay that Action (e.g. with {card:Royal Carriage} or {card:Scepter}), you won't get an additional choice on the second play.
If Elder plays a card with choices, and that card was played using {card:Way of the Chameleon}, you both get an extra choice from that card, and switch +Cards / {coin:+}.
If you use Elder on a {card:Reckless} card that gives choices, you can get an extra choice during both iterations.
Even though the word "choose" is used, Elder has no effect on cards such as {card:Advisor}, {card:Necromancer}, {card:Pillage}, {card:Swindler}, or a second Elder.
First draw 3 cards; then see if drawing those cards caused you to shuffle. If it did, you get +1 Action and +2 Favors.
It only counts as shuffling if at least one card was in your discard pile.

This checks if any cards were in your discard pile, and not how many cards were actually shuffled. So if you use either {card:Order of Astrologers} or {card:Order of Masons} to effectively shuffle 0 cards back into your deck, you'll still get the bonus from Emissary.

This checks if its +3 Cards is the effect that you makes you shuffle. So if playing Emissary gets you +1 Card from {card:Pathfinding}, and that makes you shuffle, you won't get the bonus from Emissary.

children.text: But if you use Order of Masons to leave yourself with less than 3 cards in your deck after {card:Pathfinding}, then Emissary's +3 Cards will make you shuffle, and that'll give you +1 Action and +2 Favors.

Treasures are Actions for all purposes.

children.text: For example if you use {card:Rice Broker} to trash a {card:Copper}, it's an Action and still a Treasure, so you draw 7 cards total.

items.text: Treasures can still be played in the Buy phase to do what they normally do, but if played in the Action phase, they produce +1 Card and +1 Action rather than everything they normally do.
You can turn these Treasures sideways to remind yourself that they didn't make {cost:}.
Since Treasures are Actions, they can be used with Ways (from Menagerie) to get something other than +1 Card and +1 Action.
{card:Highwayman} (from Allies) can't stop your first Treasure from being used in an Action phase for +1 Card and +1 Action.

If you use a card like {card:Black Market}, {card:Storyteller}, or {card:Herb Gatherer} to play a Treasure in the Action phase, it will still give you +1 Card and +1 Action instead of its usual effect.

Enlightenment even applies to Treasure cards that are already Actions; if you play {card:Crown}, {card:Coronet}, or an Action affected by {card:Capitalism} in the Action phase, you still get +1 Card and +1 Action instead of the card's usual effect.

children.text: However, a Treasure that is already an Action does not have its types changed by Enlightenment; an Action–Treasure doesn't become an "Action–Action–Treasure". A card either has a type or it doesn't.

items.text: Enlightenment only affects cards and not piles. This means that the Copper pile is not an Action pile for e.g. {card:Training} or {card:Populate}.
Treasures still remain as Actions when scoring (for e.g. {card:Vineyard}).

Enlightenment prevents you from following the Treasure's instructions. If you play a Treasure as {card:Way of the Chameleon}, it makes you follow its instructions (unlike the other Ways), which means Enlightenment will stop that and make you get +1 Card and +1 Action instead.

children.text: This only applies for your Action phase. If you play a {card:Gold} as Way of the Chameleon in your Buy phase, you get +3 Cards.

items.text: If you've been attacked by Highwayman and you *want* the first Treasure played in your Action phase to have no effect instead of giving you +1 Card and +1 Action, for some reason, you are permitted to allow the Highwayman to take precedence over Enlightenment.
The 10 Kingdom card Supply piles used this game are removed, as well as an 11th pile if something added one (such as {card:Young Witch}'s Bane pile, from Cornucopia).
Ruins (from Dark Ages), {card:Potion|Potions} (from Alchemy), and {card:Platinum} and {card:Colony} (from Prosperity) are not removed.
Deal out 10 new Kingdom cards.
Do any Setup for them that they require, including things like putting out the Potions if necessary.

children.text: Do not give out Heirlooms (from Nocturne).
Do not re-determine whether or not to use Shelters (from Dark Ages) or Platinum and Colony.

items.text: The removed piles are gone; they no longer count as empty piles if empty, and cards can't be returned to those piles. Players can continue playing with cards they got from those piles though.

children.text: Tokens on the removed piles are no longer on them (such as tokens from {card:Teacher}, from Adventures).
Traits (from Plunder) and {card:Obelisk} (from Empires) still affect their removed piles, and the Bane (for Young Witch) is still the Bane.

items.text: {card:Search} (from Plunder) does not trigger when piles are removed.
"In games using this" abilities, like {card:Shaman}'s (from Plunder), continue to function for removed piles.
Any cards that were involved in the original kingdom but not in the Supply (like {card:Ferryman}'s pile, {card:Riverboat}'s card, {card:Page}'s upgrades, etc.) are not removed after Divine Wind.
If a singular card has already been used in the original kingdom (e.g. it was used by Riverboat, or it was in the {card:Black Market} deck), the pile cannot be one of the 10 new piles.

Removed Adventures tokens return to their player (and they can place the token again). Any other tokens (e.g. {vp:} for {card:Farmers' Market}, or tokens for {card:Family of Inventors}) are removed forever.
Players only get an initial Favor token the first time a Liaison is added to the game. If the original kingdom had a Liaison, and Divine Wind adds another one, you don't do that setup again.

You can't exchange cards with a removed pile. That means, for example, if you have a {card:Peasant} still in your deck when the Divine Wind blows through, you won't be able to be able to replace it with a {card:Soldier}, and if you have a {card:Vampire} it will no longer be able to turn into a {card:Bat} (or vice versa).

children.text: Cards not in the Supply are not removed, so you can still exchange your Soldier for a {card:Fugitive}.

items.text: Cost reduction does not apply to cards that aren't yet in the game. This means if you play {card:Highway} and then activate Divine Wind, the cost reduction does not apply when Young Witch chooses its Bane.
A {card:Druid} in the original kingdom will keep its 3 Boons after Divine Wind happens. A Druid added in the new kingdom will set aside whatever 3 Boons are on top of the deck.

children.text: If there aren't enough Boons left (e.g. too many are set aside due to {card:Blessed Village}), Druid sets aside as many as possible.

Reveal cards from the top of your deck until you reveal a Treasure or Action card.

It only applies for the turn you buy it.
If you play {card:Outpost} (from Seaside), getting an extra turn with only 3 cards, and also buy Expedition, you add the 2 extra cards onto the base of 3 cards, for 5 cards total.

The first time this is played, it produces {coin:+1} (and +1 Buy), the next time {coin:+2}, then {coin:+3}, then {coin:+4}, then the next time the player takes the {vp:4} (and gets no {coin:+}), then the next time it is back to {coin:+1}.
This still functions if the Farmers' Market pile is empty.

If you gain this from {card:Black Market}, or when it's set aside with {card:Way of the Mouse}, there is no Farmers' Market pile. This means no {vp:} tokens will accumulate, and you won't get any {coin:+}; the card does nothing but +1 Buy.
If you play this with a Command variant, the Farmers' Market will fail to trash itself, but you still take {vp:4}.
"End of turn" is after drawing in Clean-up.

The Reaction ability can happen on your turn and on other players' turns; if for example you discard Faithful Hound to another player's {card:Raider}, you can set it aside and return it to your hand at the end of that turn.
Faithful Hound does not have to be in your hand for the ability to work; for example you can set it aside when it is discarded from your deck due to {card:Night Watchman}.

The ability does not work if Faithful Hound is put into your discard pile without being discarded; for example nothing special happens when you gain Faithful Hound, or put your deck into your discard pile with {card:Scavenger} (from Dark Ages).
The ability does not do anything during Clean-up.
Setting Faithful Hound aside is optional.
You cannot choose to discard Faithful Hound without something telling you to discard.
If you discard Faithful Hound with {card:Vassal} and choose to set it aside, {card:Vassal} will fail to play it.
{card:Deluded}/{card:Envious} is two-sided; take it with the Envious side face up.
The revealed cards that are not Actions are shuffled back into your deck.
When all revealed cards are Actions, you still shuffle your deck.

children.text: If your deck is empty after you discard the Actions and you have no cards return to your deck, you simply do nothing—you do not shuffle your discard pile to form a new deck.

items.text: This causes {card:Silver} and {card:Gold} to make {cost:1} when you [play them] in your Buy phase for one turn, rather than their usual {cost:2} and {cost:3}, starting in the Buy phase.
It does not affect other Treasures, just Silver and Gold.
If you get Envious during your turn before the Buy phase (such as with {card:Leprechaun}), it will apply that turn; normally it will apply to your next turn.
Silvers and Golds played before your Buy phase, such as by {card:Storyteller}, are not affected.
Once you return Envious, it will affect your Silvers and Golds for the rest of the turn, even if you return to the Action phase with {card:Villa} or {card:Cavalry} and then start a new Buy phase.
If you don't follow the instructions of a Silver or Gold (due to {card:Enlightenment} or {card:Highwayman}), Envious will have no effect.
If both Envious and Enlightenment are active and you play a Silver in your Buy phase as {card:Way of the Chameleon}, you will only get +1 Card.
The Spirits are {card:Will-o'-Wisp}, {card:Imp}, and {card:Ghost}.
If for example you trash a {card:Silver}, you can gain a Will-o'-Wisp or Imp, as those both cost less than Silver.
When you play this, you get +2 Cards and +1 Action, and return it to its Supply pile.
When you gain it, you gain another one; this applies whether you gain it via buying it or some other way.
If you gain one to a place other than your discard pile, the 2nd copy goes to your discard pile.

children.text: For example if you use {card:Sculptor} to gain Experiment, you get one in your hand, and one in your discard pile.

items.text: If Experiment somehow is not in play (for example if played from the trash via {card:Necromancer}, from Nocturne), it fails to return to its pile.
If you gain an Experiment from the trash, the second Experiment is still gained from the Supply.

If Experiment has no Supply pile to return to (e.g. it was acquired via {card:Black Market} or was played through {card:Way of the Mouse}) it remains in play and will remain in your custody like any other card.
You simply have +1 Buy on each of your turns.
This only cares if you gained a card in your Buy phase, whether bought, or gained other ways, such as via the {card:Treasure Chest}.
It does not count cards gained in your Action phase, such as with {card:Inventor}.
For example if all you buy on your turn is Exploration, you will get +1 Coffers and +1 Villager that turn.
In rare cases (such as with {card:Villa}, from Empires), your Buy phase can end multiple times in a turn; Exploration will happen each time it ends.
This only cares if you bought a card in your Buy phase; it does not care if you gained cards other ways, or if you bought an Event (from Adventures and Empires) or Project.
For example if all you buy on your turn is Exploration, you will get +1 Coffers and +1 Villager that turn.

Unlike {card:Hermit}, Exploration only checks if you bought any cards in the current Buy phase, and not over the whole turn. So if you buy a card from the {card:Black Market} in your Action phase and then buy nothing in your Buy phase, you'll get the tokens from Exploration, but you can't get a {card:Madman}.

If you have multiple Buy phases in a single turn (due to Villa or {card:Cavalry}), Exploration will trigger at the end of each of those Buy phases you take. Cards bought in a previous Buy phase are not counted.
This can only gain cards from the Supply.
You can react with this to any gained card with 2 or more types; it can be a card that was bought, or a card gained some other way, such as via a Falconer.
You can do this regardless of who gained the card - you or anyone else - and regardless of whose turn it is.
The types are the words on the bottom line – including Action, Attack, Curse, Duration, Reaction, Treasure, and Victory (with more in other expansions).
If you gain a Falconer to your hand - such as via {card:Artisan} - you can react to that gain and play it, since it has two types.
See the Reactions section.

If another player gains a card with 2 or more types during your turn (e.g. you give them a {card:Survivors} with {card:Cultist}), multiple players get to react with Falconer. Since it is your turn, you get to react first.

{card:Capitalism} and {card:Inheritance} can change the number of types a card has, and Falconer takes that into account when counting types. These changes are in effect on the turns of players who have bought Capitalism and Inheritance. This means that, for example, if you have Inheritance and your opponent doesn't, and you gain an {card:Estate} on your opponent's turn for some reason, Falconer isn't triggered.
{card:Charlatan} makes {card:Curse|Curses} also count as treasures, so making an opponent gain a Curse will let you play Falconer.

This can't put tokens on Victory piles. It can put tokens on split piles that have Victory cards in them, if the randomizer isn't a Victory card; this means it can put tokens on the 6 split piles in Allies, but not on the {card:Castles} pile from Empires.
The effect is cumulative; two tokens on a pile means that cards in that pile cost {cost:2} less.
This does not reduce costs below {cost:0}.
This makes cards cost less at all times for all players, not just for the player placing the token.
This can put a token on {card:Knights}, even if the top Knight in the pile is {card:Dame Josephine}.
This is mandatory.
Each time you shuffle, you can choose to put Fated cards on the top or bottom of your deck, while shuffling the other cards normally.

children.text: If for example you had five Fated cards, you could put two on top, one on the bottom, and leave the other two to be shuffled in.

items.text: In games with Fated, you can look through your deck before shuffling, even if you're sure you don't have any Fated cards.

If you put any Fated cards on top, they go on top of the shuffled cards, not on top of your deck. And if you put any Fated cards on the bottom, they go on the bottom of the shuffled cards, not on the bottom of your deck.
If {card:Patron} is Fated, then revealing it when shuffling will give you +1 Coffers (assuming that it's an Action phase). If you reveal Patron, you have to put it either on top or bottom.
If you have Shadow cards in your deck, they go to the bottom of your deck when you shuffle; bottom-decked Fated cards can go above, below, or between Shadow cards.
This can be played in your Buy phase like other Treasures, and is worth {vp:2} at the end of the game.
Use 8 Harems/Farms for games with 2 players, 12 for games with 3 or more players.
This is both a Treasure card and a Victory card.
You can play it for 2 coins, just like a {card:Silver} card.
At the end of the game, it's worth {vp:2}.
During set-up, place 12 Harems in the Supply for a 3- or 4-player game and 8 in the Supply for a 2-player game.
Setting aside a card when you gain this is optional.
Once you do it, you have to play the card at the start of your next turn, even if you no longer want to.
Playing the Action card does not "use up" one of your Action plays for the turn.
The set aside card is face up.
When you gain a Farrier you overpaid for, you draw an extra card at end of turn per {cost:1} you overpaid.

children.text: For example you could pay for {cost:4} Farrier, and draw 2 extra cards at end of turn.

items.text: This doesn't happen if you gain a Farrier without paying for it (such as with {card:Horn of Plenty}).
The gained card goes into your Discard pile.
It has to be a card from the Supply.
You cannot use {cost:} from Treasures or previous Actions (like the {card:Market}) to increase the cost of the card that you gain.

If you use {card:Throne Room} on Feast, you will gain two cards, even though you can only trash Feast once. Gaining the card isn't contingent on trashing Feast; they're just two things that the card tries to make you do.
You get +2 Actions, +1 Buy, and {coin:+2}.

If you are playing multiple Festivals, keep a careful count of your Actions. Say how many you have left out loud; this trick works every time (i.e. "I'm playing the Festival and now have two Actions remaining. I play a Market and have two Actions remaining. I play another Festival and now have three Actions remaining….").
You get +2 Actions and {coin:+1} when you play this, and then +1 Action and {coin:+1} at the start of your next turn.
You get a coin to spend and 2 more Actions to use this turn.
At the start of your next turn you get a coin and only one more Action.
This means you will be able to play 2 Actions total on your next turn (counting your normal Action).
Leave this in front of you until the Clean-up phase of your next turn.
This is a Victory card, so use eight copies for games with two players, or 12 for games with three or more players.
At the end of the game, each Feodum is worth {vp:1} for every three {card:Silver|Silvers} in your deck, rounded down.

children.text: For example if you have 11 Silvers, your Feodums are worth {vp:3} each.

items.text: If Feodum is trashed, you gain three Silvers.
If there are not enough Silvers left, gain as many as you can.
This is a Victory card. Play with 8 for games with 2 players, or 12 cards for games with 3 or more players.
At the end of the game, each Feodum is worth 1 for every 3 Silvers in your deck, rounded down.

children.text: For example, if you have 11 Silvers, your Feodums are worth 3 each.

items.text: If a Feodum is trashed, you gain 3 Silvers.
The Silvers come from the Supply and are put into your discard pile.
If there are not enough Silvers left, gain as many as you can.
Trash a card from your hand if you can.
Whether or not you can, you still get {coin:+1} per differently named Treasure in the trash, plus +1 Action and +1 Buy.
Multiple copies of the same Treasure card do not increase how much you get.

children.text: For example if the trash has four {card:Copper|Coppers} and a {card:Counterfeit}, you get {coin:+2}.

items.text: First you trash a card, then you calculate how much {cost:} you get. The card you trash with Forager, if it is a Treasure, may contribute to this calculation.

Effects that are triggered *by* trashing a card take place before calculating your {coin:+}. For instance, if you have {card:Sewers}, and you trash a card with Forager, whereupon Sewers lets you trash an additional card, a Treasure trashed by Sewers can also figure into the calculation.

However, the amount of {cost:} Forager fields is calculated the instant after it trashes a card (once all when-trashed effects are resolved); do *not* wait until the Buy phase to check how many Treasures are in the trash.
If Treasures are removed from the trash (with e.g. {card:Treasurer}), future Foragers will give less {cost:}.
Action cards affected by {card:Capitalism} in the trash are also counted by Forager.
Trash a card from your hand if you can.
Whether or not you can, you still get {coin:+1} per differently named Treasure in the trash, plus +1 Action and +1 Buy.
Multiple copies of the same Treasure card do not increase how much you get.

children.text: For example, if the trash has four Coppers, a Counterfeit, and six {card:Estate|Estates}, you get {coin:+2}.

items.text: Cards with multiple types, one of which is Treasure (such as {card:Harem} from Intrigue), are Treasures.
Do the things in the order listed. You draw 2 cards; then you gain an {card:Estate}; then each other player (in turn order) gains a {card:Curse} and discards down to 3 cards in hand.
A player with 3 or fewer cards in hand does not discard any cards.
If there are no Estates left, you do not gain one.

Do the things in the order listed. You draw 2 cards; then you gain an Estate from the Supply, putting it into your discard pile; then each other player gains a Curse from the Supply, putting it into his discard pile; then each other player discards down to 3 cards in hand.
A player with 3 or fewer cards in hand does not discard any cards.
If there are no Estates left, you do not gain one.
If there are not enough Curses left, deal out the remaining Curses in turn order.
This is a Prize; see the Additional Rules.
The first Fool's Gold you play in a turn is makes {coin:+1}, and all further copies are make {coin:+4}.
So if you play three of them, you get {cost:1} + {cost:4} + {cost:4}, or {cost:9} total.
Fool's Gold is also a Reaction.

children.text: When another player gains a {card:Province}, you may trash Fool's Gold from your hand to gain a {card:Gold} from the Supply, putting it onto your deck.
You cannot use this ability when you gain a Province, only when another player does.

items.text: If you play the same Fool's Gold twice in the same turn (e.g., with {card:Crown} or {card:Counterfeit}), the second play will produce {coin:+4}.
If another player gains a Province during your turn (e.g. you play a {card:Governor} and they trash a {card:King's Court} into Province), you can react with your Fool's Gold.
Even if your 1st Fool's Gold gets blocked by {card:Highwayman}, your other Fool's Golds will still give {coin:+4}.
This is both a Treasure and a Reaction.
It can be played in your Buy phase like other Treasures.
When you play it, it is worth {cost:1} if this is the first time you played a Fool's Gold this turn, and otherwise it is worth {cost:4}.
So if you play three Fool's Golds in the same turn, the first is worth {cost:1}, the second is worth {cost:4}, and the third is worth {cost:4}.

Fool's Gold is also a Reaction. When another player gains a Province, you may trash Fool's Gold from your hand; if you do, you gain a Gold from the Supply, putting it on top of your deck rather than into your discard pile.
If there are no cards in your deck, the Gold becomes the only card in your deck.
If there are no Gold cards left in the Supply, you do not gain one, but can still trash Fool's Gold.
This Reaction is only usable when another player gains a Province, not you.
It is usable whether a Province was gained due to being bought, or gained some other way.
When you buy this, you move your -2 cost token to any Action Supply pile.
This token makes cards from that pile cost {cost:2} less, but not less than {cost:0}, on your turns; see the Tokens section.
Other players' cards from the tokened pile are also reduced in cost during your turns.

For split piles, the types of a pile are determined solely by the types on its randomizer card. For example, the Odysseys pile has the types Action-Odyssey, even though the cards themselves have other types. Similarly, {card:Castles} is not an Action pile even if an Action card is currently at the top of the Castles pile.
If you have {card:Lost in the Woods}, playing Fool does nothing.

If you do not have Lost in the Woods, you take it - even from another player, if another player has it - and also take 3 Boons and receive them in the order you choose (discarding them when receiving them, or in Clean-up as appropriate).
You do not need to pick the full order in advance - pick one to resolve, then after resolving it pick another to resolve.
The player with Lost in the Woods (if any) can optionally discard a card to receive a Boon, at the start of each of their turns.
In games using Fool, replace one of your starting {card:Copper|Coppers} with a {card:Lucky Coin}.
You discard an Action or Treasure if you have either, and only reveal your hand if you have no Actions and no Treasures.
When you gain or trash a Flag Bearer, you take the {card:Flag}.

The Flag causes you to draw an extra card when drawing your hand in Clean-up. This is true even if your hand would normally be some amount other than 5 cards - for example if you played {card:Outpost} (from Seaside), instead of drawing 3 cards for your Outpost turn, you would draw 4.
If Flag Bearer is trashed, the player trashing it takes the Flag, regardless of whose turn it is.
Refer to the Flag Bearer FAQ section.
The extra turns go in order starting with the next player after the one that just took a turn.

Other extra turns, such as from {card:Outpost} (in Seaside) can happen in-between those turns; however after the last extra turn due to Fleet, no other extra turns can happen (since e.g. Outpost does not keep the game going after it ends).
Players do not sort through their cards and add up their scores until all of the Fleet turns are done, even the players without Fleet.
If the game end conditions are no longer met after Fleet turns, the game is still over.
If no players have bought Fleet, the game ends before any extra turns happen from e.g. Outpost, {card:Possession}, {card:Mission}, or {card:Seize the Day}.

Fleet doesn't create extra turns; it creates an extra round of turns. This means that if you have Fleet and then get Possessed on what would be the last turn of the game, you cannot take your Fleet turn before the Possession turn.
If during your Fleet turn, you play Possession and make the next player buy Fleet for themselves, they do not get a turn with Fleet.
If you end the game and take an extra turn in the same turn, and another player has Fleet, you will get your extra turn. During that turn, if you buy Fleet, you will not get a Fleet turn.
This costs {cost:5} normally, but {cost:2} whenever the player whose turn it is has an empty discard pile.
If you have {cost:4} and two Buys with an empty discard pile, you can buy Fisherman for {cost:2}, but then you will no longer have an empty discard pile, so you cannot buy a second for {cost:2}.
See the Unusual Costs section.
You can only do this once per time you play an Action card.
Completely resolve the Action card; then if you have 4 or fewer cards in hand, you may spend a Favor for +1 Card.
When you play this, you get {coin:+3} and at the start of your next turn, you get +2 Cards.
This isn't optional; whatever that next non-Command Action card is, Flagship replays it.
It replays it even if the card trashed itself, and even if it isn't your turn.
Command cards, such as Flagship itself, are not replayed; Flagship waits for a non-Command Action card.
If you play two Flagships and then e.g. a {card:Harbor Village}, you'll play the Harbor Village three times total - once normally and once for each Flagship.
See the Additional rules section for Duration cards in Dominion: Plunder regarding things happening "the next time".

If you play a Flagship and then a {card:Band of Misfits}, you will replay the card that the {card:Band of Misfits} plays. But if you play a Flagship and then a {card:Necromancer}, Flagship will replay the Necromancer (and you'll choose a 2nd card to play from the trash).
If you don't have any Action cards to play, you'll still draw up to 6.
If the Action card you play draws you another copy of itself, you can play that copy, and so on.
First Mate can play First Mates; keep careful track of which card you're resolving, as you would with multiple {card:Throne Room|Throne Rooms}.
If you didn't have 3 cards to discard, you don't gain a Loot.
This is a Treasure, and so is played in your Buy phase, but draws cards.
This means that usually if it draws you an Action card, that card won't be useful that turn, except that Figurine itself lets you discard one Action card for +1 Buy and {coin:+1}.
In games using Ferryman, choose an additional Kingdom card costing {cost:3} or {cost:4}, and put its pile near the Supply.
This pile is not part of the Supply, and these cards can only be gained via gaining a Ferryman. Do any setup the chosen card requires.
When you gain a Ferryman, you also gain a copy of whichever card was set aside in setup.

children.text: For example in setup you might set aside {card:Shop}, which costs {cost:3}; then that game, when you gained a Ferryman, you'd also gain a Shop.

items.text: The card chosen for Ferryman can't be gained other ways, only by gaining a Ferryman.
If the chosen card is a split pile (such as the {card:Augurs} from Dominion: Allies), different cards will be gained via Ferryman gains as they get uncovered.
Do any setup required of the chosen card. So if the chosen card is {card:Young Witch}, you'll add another Kingdom pile to the Supply.
In the case of a split pile, it is the cost listed on the pile's randomizer card that determines whether it is eligible to be set aside for Ferryman.
If Ferryman is gained from the trash or from the {card:Black Market} deck, you also gain a card from the set aside pile.

If the chosen pile is e.g. {card:Odysseys}, {card:Old Map} can rotate its own pile. But if the chosen pile is {card:Clashes}, {card:Battle Plan} can't rotate it because Battle Plan specifies that the rotated pile must be in the Supply.
Contrary to the FAQ, cards like {card:Rats} can gain copies of themselves from their own pile, because it explicitly says "gain a {card:Rats}."

children.text: However, {card:Acolyte} and {card:Small Castle} can't gain cards from their pile if it isn't in the Supply. This is because instead of trying to gain a card with a specific name, they try to gain a card with a specific type (from the Supply).

items.text: {card:Changeling}'s ability still works even if it's not in the Supply (as long as any are in the pile).
{card:Temple} and {card:Farmers' Market} can add and take {vp:} from their own pile, even if it's not in the Supply.
This changes any game it's part of, even if no-one has gained a Footpad.
For that entire game, any time you gain a card in an Action phase, you draw a card.

children.text: For example if you played {card:Remake} to turn two {card:Estate|Estates} into two {card:Silver|Silvers}, you'd draw two cards.

items.text: Drawing isn't optional.
This doesn't draw you cards in Buy phases or Clean-up, just Action phases.
When you play a Footpad, you get +2 Coffers, and the other players discard down to 3 cards in hand.
See the Shadows section.
When you play Fishmonger, you get +1 Buy and {coin:+1}.
If you have bought {card:Capitalism}, you can also play Fishmonger from your deck whenever you could normally play Treasures from your hand.
The cost lowering applies to all cards everywhere, including cards in the Supply, in hands, and in Decks.
It's cumulative with other things that lower costs, like {card:Bridge} from Intrigue.
If you have Action plays left in your Buy phase, you can use them as Buys instead.
For example if you play no Actions at all, you have one Action play you didn't use, and so can use that as an extra Buy.
What's relevant here is Action plays, not Action cards; you get one Action play per turn normally, and can increase that with cards like {card:Rustic Village}.
Cards still cost {cost:1} less when scoring (which matters for {card:Plateau Shepherds}).
The card is added to your hand after drawing your next hand.
For example, if you have 37 cards at the end of the game, each copy of Gardens you have is worth {vp:3}.
Use 8 copies of Gardens in a 2-player game, 12 copies for 3 or more players.

Gardens counts all the cards belonging to you, including cards you have in play, cards that you have set aside, and cards on your mats, in addition to those physically in your deck at the end of the game.
This Kingdom card is a Victory card, not an Action card.

It does nothing until the end of the game, when it is worth 1 victory point per 10 cards in your Deck (counting all of your cards – your Discard pile and hand are combined with your Deck before scoring).
Round down; if you have 39 cards, Gardens is worth 3 victory points.
During set-up, place 12 Gardens in the Supply for a 3 or 4 player game and 8 in the Supply for a 2 player game.
Each other player keeps putting cards from their hand onto their deck, in any order they choose, until they only have 3 cards in hand.
Players who already had 3 or fewer cards in hand do not put any cards onto their deck.
The other players choose which cards they put on their decks and in what order.
This has no effect on another player who already has only 3 cards in hand.
A player with no cards left in their deck does not shuffle; the cards put back become the only cards in their deck.
Each other player reveals cards from the top of their deck until they reveal a Victory or {card:Curse} card.
If they do not find one (even after shuffling), they just discard all of the revealed cards.
If they do find one, they put the Victory or Curse card on top of their deck, and discard the other revealed cards.
You do not choose Victory or Curse - they stop on the first card that matches either type.
Cards with Victory as one of multiple types, such as {card:Nobles}, are still Victory cards and can be left on top by Fortune Teller.
Each other player reveals cards from the top of his deck until he reveals a Victory or Curse card.
If he runs out of cards before finding one, he shuffles his discard pile (but not the revealed cards), and keeps revealing cards.
If he still cannot find one, he just discards all of the revealed cards.
If he does find one, he puts the Victory or Curse card on top of his deck, and discards the other revealed cards.
If his deck has no other cards in it, it becomes the only card in his deck.
A card with multiple types, one of which is Victory (such as {card:Nobles} from Dominion: Intrigue), is a Victory card.
You do not choose Victory or Curse - they stop on the first card that matches either type.
"Any number" includes zero.
If you trash no cards, you have to gain a card costing {cost:0} if you can.
If there is no card at the required cost, you do not gain a card.
The card you gain comes from the Supply and is put into your discard pile.
{potion} (on cards in Dominion: Alchemy) and {debt:} (on cards in Dominion: Empires) are not added, and the card you gain cannot have those symbols in its cost.
"Any number" includes zero.
If you trash no cards, you have to gain a card costing {cost:0} if you can.
This is different from how cards like {card:Expand} work if you do not trash anything, because Forge looks at the total, not at any one card's cost.
If there is no card at the required cost, you do not gain a card.

The card you gain comes from the Supply and is put into your discard pile. {potion} symbols (on cards from Dominion: Alchemy) are not added, and the card you gain cannot have a {potion} symbol in its cost.
When you play this, you draw a card and get +2 Actions.
If this is trashed, you take it from the trash and put it into your hand.
This happens no matter whose turn it is when Fortress is trashed.
It is not optional.
You still trashed Fortress, even though you got it back; for example if you play {card:Death Cart} and choose to trash Fortress, you did trash it and so get {coin:+5}.
When you put Fortress in your hand after trashing it, it is not 'gained': you just put it in your hand. You can't reveal {card:Trader} or {card:Watchtower} to do something else with it.

If a {card:Possession|Possessed} player's Fortress is trashed, the Possessing player chooses whether to put it back in hand immediately, as usual, or to set it aside with other trashed cards, to be returned to the Possessed player's discard pile at the end of the turn.
If you trash a Fortress from the Supply with {card:Lurker}, you put the Fortress into your hand; it still doesn't count as being "gained".
When you play this, you draw a card and get +2 Actions.
If this is trashed, you take it from the trash and put it into your hand.
This happens no matter whose turn it is when Fortress is trashed.
It is not optional.

You still trashed Fortress, even though you get it back; for example if you play Death Cart and choose to trash Fortress, the "if you do" on Death Cart is true, you did trash an Action, so you do not trash Death Cart.
At the start of the game, your Journey token () is face up.
When you play this, you turn it over.
Then, if it is face down, you get {coin:+1} and nothing more happens.
If it is face up, you get {coin:+5} and the attack part happens.
